text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mystery surrounds how needles were found to be in a young girl's body. The welfare department knew about the case 11 months ago.
- A dispute breaks out in the Greek government on the Cyprus problem and Greek-Turkish disputes.
- Increases in insurance premiums comes under scrutiny by the House of Representatives.
- Police step in as a fourth needle is found in a baby's brain.
- Proximity talks on military issues go on despite crisis reports.
- Communist Akel general secretary Demetris Christofias says he is confident of a win in next month's municipal elections.
- Suspending military flights over Cyprus is a political, not military issue, says the government.
- Doctors and nursing staff threaten strikes at government hospitals over poor staffing levels.
- Commission investigating tender procedures in the state-run electricity authority will have meetings open to the public.
- Attorney-general is expected to announce whether policemen will be prosecuted in connection with a murder and a murder attempt last year.
